tests.name: a 529 result is overloaded, not the account's failure

No production behavior change or replacement case.

contractSources.contract: Repeated529 overloads arrive as success-subtype results carrying api_error_status529.
Claude529 is stamped reason overloaded, retried without account cooldown/switch, never account failover.
RuntimeFailureReason overload is provider-capacity failure, distinct from account usage_limit/auth.

tests.name: a terminal serverOverloaded ("Selected model is at capacity") is overloaded, never while retrying
tests.reason: Unique raw Codex serverOverloaded mapping and provider-retry suppression: the same protocol code must carry no actionable reason while willRetry=true, then overloaded when terminal. Existing usage/auth tests and normalized notice/recovery tests do not own this mapping.

contractSources.contract: Generated provider protocol declares serverOverloaded as its own code, distinct from usageLimitExceeded/rateLimitExceeded/unauthorized.
Retryable provider errors are warnings; terminal errors are surfaced. A retry which may succeed is not acted upon as a stopped chat.
Codex Selected model is at capacity/serverOverloaded becomes overloaded and retries shortly without account cooldown/switch.
Canonical overload reason identifies provider capacity rather than account failure.

sixBar.independentContract: Raw serverOverloaded becomes canonical overloaded only when provider marks the failure terminal; in-flight provider retry must not trigger host capacity recovery.
sixBar.recognizableFailure: Capacity-stopped Codex chat never retries, is switched/cooled as a quota account, or host recovery races an in-flight provider retry.
sixBar.independentOracle: Literal [undefined,"overloaded"] for explicit willRetry true/false inputs; no classifier output or production constants calculate expected values. Helper message still mentions429, usefully checking structured codexErrorInfo wins over message wording.
sixBar.stableSeam: Production-used CodexNormaliser.notification consumes raw generated-protocol error frames; case inspects canonical error/warning payload reason.
sixBar.refactorResistance: No private failureReasonOf import, call-count assertion, implementation inventory, snapshot or exact error prose; internal dispatch/classifier refactors preserve protocol inputs and emitted reason.
sixBar.uniqueProtection: Existing generic retry case uses usageLimitExceeded and cannot catch missing serverOverloaded classification or code-specific premature overload annotation. API/daemon retry tests use normalized activity; they cannot replace provider-code mapping. Both statuses are one cheap scenario.
